_note: Copy of config.example.json. The setup interview (/job-search setup) fills this in for you; you can also edit it by hand. Keys starting with _ are notes and are ignored. Everything here is a fictional example candidate (Alex Morgan, a senior pre-sales Solutions Engineer in cloud-native observability, home base Austin, TX).

profile._note: Who the application-prep and analysis prompts are written for. Paths may start with ~.
profile.search_scope: a senior remote-US (or Austin, TX) role
profile._proof_note: One true, measurable sentence used in warm-intro notes, e.g. 'I run technical validations that win about 70% of proofs of concept.' Leave empty to omit it.

angles._note: Angles are the labels shown on each job (and used for conversion stats). 'terms' are theme words that make the rules-only scorer pick that angle; 'describe' tells the model what the label means. Edit freely: the setup interview writes angles in your field's language.

list.name: Observability
list.describe: observability, monitoring, incident response or AIOps products for cloud-native and DevOps teams

list.name: Cloud-native
list.describe: Kubernetes, containers, platform engineering or DevOps tooling

list.name: Other
list.describe: the core product is none of these

judge._note: Plain-English definition the scoring model uses. core_theme says what counts as a strong match.
judge.core_theme: the role centers on observability, monitoring or incident-response products, Kubernetes and cloud-native platforms, DevOps or SRE tooling, or AI infrastructure and MLOps, sold to enterprise customers
judge._engineering_note: true drops pure software/ML/backend engineering roles (right for customer-facing roles). Set false if engineering roles are what you want.

watch_no_api._note: Companies with no readable job-board feed. Each run, Claude WebFetches the careers URL (works only where the page isn't JavaScript-rendered).

public_job_pages._note: Optional. Boards whose API lists postings but whose own pages 404. Key = source label; link pattern uses {slug}.

targeting._title_skip_note: A title containing any of these words is dropped. Add seniority or region words you never want.
targeting._home_note: Cities/areas where an in-person or hybrid role is acceptable. Substring match on the location field. Ambiguous town names should carry the state, e.g. 'georgetown, tx'.
targeting._territory_note: Words in a posting's territory (e.g. 'Territory: South Central') that mean the role covers where you live. Roles whose territory names only other regions are dropped.
targeting._salary_note: Base floor in USD. A posting is dropped only when the TOP of its stated base range is below salary_floor (if only OTE is stated, the top of the OTE range must reach ote_floor). salary_bonus_at earns a score point. Postings with no stated pay are kept.
targeting._domain_note: domain_strong terms each add a score point (up to scoring.domain_hit_max); domain_weak terms only help break ties. Use the words that appear in postings you would want.
targeting._age_note: Postings older than max_age_days are dropped; aggregator feeds use max_age_days_feeds.
targeting._excluded_note: Companies you never want to see (names, case-insensitive). The dashboard can add to this when you Pass a job and choose Exclude company.

scoring._pay_note: post_sales_adjust and tam_adjust subtract points from roles that are mainly support/delivery or Technical Account Manager roles. Set both to 0 if that distinction does not apply to you.

jobs_file._note: How tidy organizes jobs.md. Which statuses archive and when follow-ups are due live in scripts/statuses.py.

automation._note: Settings for scripts/run_cycle.py (the scheduled entry point). These are spending caps in US dollars per run: judge_budget_usd (scoring new postings) and discover_budget_usd (web discovery). Raise or lower them; --no-llm runs rules-only for free.
